subject: Resolver trust-chain audit & mTLS rotation plan — FinMark private deploy
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Tim Barnes <tim.barnes@finmark.io>
Cc: FinMark Infra <it-infra@finmark.io>
Date: Thu, 07 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Resolver trust-chain audit & mTLS rotation plan — FinMark private deploy

Hi team,

Following our onboarding call last week, I want to capture the open decisions around private DNS/resolver ownership and certificate provenance for FinMark's single-tenant VPC deployment. The goals are to:

- Ensure name-assertion and FQDN ownership is provable for auditors (supporting SOC2/PCI needs).
- Define who operates the authoritative resolver and how split-horizon rules are enforced.
- Agree an mTLS rotation cadence and root-anchor custody (ACME vs. offline-root).
- Specify telemetry/audit logs we need for cert issuance/OCSP stapling and KV-cache invalidation.

High-level options we discussed:
1) FinMark-managed resolver (their VPC resolver forwards to Redwood only for service records). Root anchor stays in FinMark HSM. Redwood issues leaf certs (ACME or CSR pipeline) and rotates monthly.
2) Redwood-managed resolver stub in customer's VPC (we operate an ephemeral resolver/sidecar). Redwood-controlled ACME for leaf certs; FinMark retains offline root with signed intermediates.

Key questions for FinMark:
- Who will retain the root trust? (HSM in FinMark or Redwood-managed root with MOA)
- Are you comfortable with an ACME-issued ephemeral leaf cert model (short-lived certs + OCSP stapling) or do you require signed CSRs with manual signing?
- Audit requirements: minimum retention window for issuance logs and OCSP responses (we suggested 13 months to match typical compliance windows).

I've attached the resolver diagram (finmark_resolver_diagram_v2.png) and a proposed CSR/rotation matrix (csr_rotation_matrix.xlsx). Please reply with preferences; once we have alignment we'll draft the MOA for root-anchor custody and a 30/60/90-day rollout plan for rotation.

Thanks,
Karthik

On Thu, 07 Oct 2026 at 09:12 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Following our onboarding call last week, I want to capture the open decisions around private DNS/resolver ownership and certificate provenance for FinMark's single-tenant VPC deployment.

Bringing a couple of implementation points into the thread:
- If FinMark keeps the authoritative resolver, we will need a signed proof-of-assertion: either DNSSEC-signed NS delegation or a signed JSON statement (timestamped) that we store in our audit bucket.
- For the leaf cert lifecycle, our runtime supports automatic OCSP stapling and short-lived certs down to 24 hours; the ops trade-off is more frequent CSR churn vs. simpler revocation semantics.

Marissa

From: Tim Barnes <tim.barnes@finmark.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 08 Oct 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Resolver trust-chain audit & mTLS rotation plan — FinMark private deploy

Thanks Karthik — useful summary. A few firm responses from FinMark infra: 

- Root custody: FinMark will keep the root in our on-prem HSM (FIPS 140-2 Level 3). We will provide a signed anchor (PDF + digest) and will sign an intermediate for Redwood to use. We do not want Redwood to hold our root.
- Resolver ownership: FinMark runs the authoritative resolver inside the VPC. We can add an NS delegation for the redwood-internal subzone (svc.finmark.internal) and provide DNSSEC-signed delegations. We expect Redwood to fetch and archive the delegation proof as part of the onboarding audit.
- Certificate issuance: We accept ACME for short-lived leaf certs if Redwood can show CSR provenance and store all ACME/issuance logs. Alternatively, we can accept a CSR pipeline where FinMark's CA signs the CSR; both are acceptable.
- Rotation cadence: Prefer monthly rotation for intermediates used by Redwood and weekly for leaf certs where feasible.
- Audit & retention: We require issuance/OCSP logs retained for 18 months. OCSP stapling must be visible in the connection traces we receive from Redwood (per-route).

Action items from our side: attaching the MOA template for the root-anchor (moa_finmark_root_anchor.pdf). We'll also share an export of our resolver's DNSSEC key slots once legal signs the MOA.

Regards,
Tim Barnes
Head of Infra, FinMark
tim.barnes@finmark.io
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tim Barnes <tim.barnes@finmark.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Resolver trust-chain audit & mTLS rotation plan — FinMark private deploy

Tim — excellent, thanks for the clarity. Summary of next steps (owner in parens):

1) FinMark legal to sign MOA for root-anchor custody (FinMark). We will not hold your root.
2) FinMark infra to provide DNSSEC-signed NS delegations for svc.finmark.internal and the DNSSEC key export (FinMark).
3) Redwood to implement issuance pipeline: accept FinMark-signed intermediate OR run ACME with full issuance logging. We'll prototype ACME + CSR provenance flow and present logs (Redwood / Marissa).
4) Rotation policy: Redwood to schedule weekly leaf rotation and monthly intermediate rotation; engineering to provide a rollback plan for 0–72 hour certificate recovery (Redwood / Karthik + Grace).
5) Audit storage: Redwood to retain issuance and OCSP records for 18 months (Redwood / Ops). We'll provide an S3 AR encryption approach and access logs for their auditors.

I've opened INF-3421 in Jira for the engineering track and uploaded the diagram and CSR matrix. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3421

Marissa — can you draft the initial ACME + CSR provenance design doc and share by EOD next Tuesday? Grace — please scope the rollback runbook and the telemetry changes to include per-route stapled OCSP visibility.

Tim — once FinMark uploads the DNSSEC proof and signatory, we'll generate a short PoC: a signed assertion object + timestamped zip of the issuance logs for your auditors.

Thanks all — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Director, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
